title: Saints RB Audric Estime on getting back into the offense, hunger to get a win against Browns
text: We did a great job this week.  Um, I feel like everyone in this building really wants to win, and I'll do whatever is asked of me.  Whatever my level of responsibility, I will try to make the most of my role to help the team win. You know, the NFL can be a strange and complicated business, but how much have you been looking forward to coming back here? Oh, yes, 100%.  As I've said since I got back, I feel like New Orleans is my home.  Since I arrived here last year, I have been welcomed with open arms, I feel like I can succeed here, I feel confident and I am just glad to be back. So, were you able to easily integrate back into the team's game? Yes, 100%.  This transition was so easy that it didn't even feel like a transition.  I think I was only gone for a month, but I'm back because I know all the combinations.  I know that Taysom and I have good chemistry, as do the offensive line, so it was very easy. What has this journey been like: from being here in camp, on the injured list, an injury deal, changing teams a few times, and now here again?  What was this trip like? It certainly wasn't easy.  But I sincerely believe that everything in life happens for a reason .  I feel like I needed to go on this little tour.  I call this the tour that got me to where I am today, and it made me hungrier, made me not take things for granted, and I'm just happy to be here.  I feel like this is where I was meant to be from the beginning, and I'm so excited to be How much football, particularly Saints games, have you watched from a distance, and what problems have you seen that you think could be fixed with your involvement? Um, I hardly watched anything because I was busy playing.  I had to focus on my work, so to be honest , I didn't watch anything.   I think I only watched the Atlanta game on Monday night because we didn't play that day .  It was Monday, but other than that , I was just focused on my work. Calvin talked about the coaching changes and the things they did this week, well, changing the approach dramatically, fundamentally.  When you returned, did you notice any small adjustments that you liked?   The big change I see is that everyone is hungry.  Everyone strives to win. I feel like we're all on the same page. Everyone knows what our mission and task are, and I feel like people just want to win and succeed, and I think that will take us far. What was the atmosphere like at training this week?  Was this aggression?  Is it possible to perform?  What was the atmosphere like at training? Yes, it was more focused on execution.  Our coaches came in on Wednesday with a great game plan and really focused on the small details and getting off to a fast start. We started training quickly.  We started the breakdown quickly and it was a great week, I'm just looking forward to what we show on Sunday.

title: Coach Harbaugh Interview: J.J. McCarthy's Growth and Team's Work During the Bye | New York Giants
text: It is a great pleasure to welcome New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh. The coach had the opportunity to recharge his batteries a bit during the rest week.  Tell us about the work you were able to accomplish during that week. Well, the most important thing was the group effort, you know, it was in two parts: the players and the coaches. We worked with the players a little at the beginning of the week.  In the weight room, during recovery, as well as during practices and meetings.  And then, afterwards , they had free time. He knows, his job was to recover, to heal the blows, the bruises and even the emotional scars. And simply rejuvenate for the next part that's coming up. Then, the coaches were doing a continuous analysis of ourselves throughout the season and we put all those reports together . We studied those reports and, before leaving, we drew up a plan to apply what we had learned to the games ahead. Coach, I saw you in the locker room after the game and told you that there were no penalties for procedural fouls throughout the entire game. And they have a new quarterback, right?  There are many different pieces, but he also came from a match where he said we needed to improve. What was that feeling like when you reviewed the video, since you said you had to check it ?  When he returned and saw that. Exact.  I mean, it's a very important thing, as you know, and the fact that you pointed it out, I hadn't realized it .  It wasn't something that caught my attention at the time.  I guess it was like they say: what you don't see, you do n't feel.   We did n't have those kinds of setbacks, and not having them makes all the difference in continuing to move forward and maintain the pace of play. So he was an important part of that game and we should take advantage of it.  It will be a difficult environment in Philadelphia.  It's going to be noisy.  It's going to be deafening.  It's going to be a challenging defense.  We need to build on that. Coach, many players commented that the team meeting after the previous match was a bit tough, right?  Because you didn't play at the level that was expected. Receiving that message must have been music to your ears, that the boys understood what you were preaching. Yes, and that's the important thing, we need to have honest football talks and that's what we did. We had honest football talks and our boys, our boys are strong, you know, they're tough.  They can handle honesty, and that's the only way to improve. Is that one of the keys to your long and successful career, that players look for honesty?  Sometimes it might not be what a player wants to hear, but as long as you're honest with the group, they usually respond. Yes, I think it's double, just like what you 're saying.  They want you to speak to them directly and tell them the truth , but they also want to know that you are on their side and that you want to see them succeed .  I mean, those two things are really important.  If not... I mean, if you're a coach and you're not on the side of your players, if you don't want to see them do well, then what are you doing?  I mean, they're your boys, so you have to be on their side, but part of supporting them is loving them and caring enough about them to tell them the truth. Coach, I want to talk a little bit about J.J.  McCarthy.  You prepared him for his first full game as a New York Giant. After that match, what's the process now?   Do you continue to focus on the mechanics, or do you say, "Okay, we see more of what it can do"?   Does that mean, "Okay, maybe we can do a little more than this"? You really get to know a player when you're around them in person all the time; otherwise, you don't really know the guy.  Even in a video, you think you know a player, but that's not the case until you see him in person, until you see what he 's capable of.  So we 're still learning that with J.J.  And honestly, with all our guys.  You keep learning that as you go, but that's part of it, and also understanding that the chess game has begun. You know, now there will be a give and take. Our defensive coordinator is going to plan the game against what we did offensively against Houston. So, what's our next move and how are we going to...how is that battle going to play out?   The coach mentioned self-analysis.  Did you enjoy any free time? Oh, yes, of course.  We have, we have some time. Halloween weekend, too. Halloween weekend, we went out, kids were trick-or-treating, you know, we had fun. We're giving away Mark Bavaro bobbleheads, so you know, it was... I don't know, we got a box of them, so we're sharing them. Very good, coach.  You trained there , you know what the atmosphere is like. Lincoln Financial Field may not be the Vet, but it's still a pretty tough place to play. Um, what will it be like to wear the rival's colors for the first time in the division?   We'll see , we've been there wearing rival colors, but not those of the Giants.  It's a little different.  He knows, he often says that there is a select group of people blessed to play this sport. And when you look at a team's win-loss record, yours or anyone else's, the margin of error and the difference between one team and another isn't that big, and people, because of the record, assume: "Hey, these guys have no talent."  But there are only a few people in this world who can do this.  So there is talent on every team .   That's exactly right.  I say that's a fallacy.  I mean, the point difference, that's why... I don't know, that's why people don't win all their bets.  Yes. I mean, you never know, we were underdogs by ten and a half points last week , we took that and maybe used it to motivate ourselves, but the point is, all these players are great.  All these teams are great.  They fight for , they fight for just this much.  I look at teams that...there are a couple of teams that haven't won a game yet.  I promise you they are very good football teams. Coach, while studying Philadelphia to prepare for this game, they've had a ton of injuries, haven't they ?  You lose a Super Bowl-winning quarterback, Saquon has been hit hard.  Do you analyze the concepts of what they want to do and say, "Okay, whoever you have available, these are the concepts they like to execute "? Undoubtedly, but you more or less know who will be available to a certain extent. I mean, there are only a couple of guys who will be there day in and day out and who might not even play.  You know who's outside.  Saquon should be healthy.  You know, he's been working on that hamstring for a few weeks now.  He's been playing for the last few weeks.  The defense is healthy.  In other words, the entire defense is there playing, actually.  I mean, there's always one or two missing, but they have their entire defense there.  They are at full strength for the most part.  So, the fact that the quarterback isn't there , that does matter.  But we understand that our quarterback isn't there either. So you play with the next man and we've done that too.  That's just football in the National Football League. Carl, I saw the recordings of the coaches watching Carter and what he can do up front, and Davis.  Those guys can ruin a game.  They almost ruined the Jacksonville game all by themselves What makes them such a big challenge ?   They're dominant physical factors, you know.  I mean, they're monsters.  They're football monsters out there .  They are big, strong, play head-on, and use their hands well.  We respect the way they play.  They play the way we taught our defense.  They play facing forwards and handle blocks well. They can handle two blocks, break free, and make plays.   They are also a force in the pass rush and have others on the outside pressing and moving. Yes, they have a complete defense.  There is no doubt about that.  Very talented. It's a short week, obviously, with Washington on Thursday. Good luck this week against Philadelphia.
